jobs.title: Deputy Director, Jewish Community Relations Council
jobs.description:
Department: Jewish Community Relations Council

Location: Miami, FL

Employment Type: Full-time / Exempt / Hybrid

***Job Description Summary***

The Greater Miami Jewish Federation seeks a strategic, relationship-driven and highly motivated professional to serve as Deputy Director of its Jewish Community Relations Council (JCRC).

The JCRC serves as the public affairs and community relations arm of the Greater Miami Jewish Federation, building relationships and coalitions that strengthen the Jewish community, combat antisemitism, deepen understanding of Israel and the Jewish people, and advance the Jewish community’s interests and values in the broader civic community.

The Deputy Director will serve as a senior operational lead of the JCRC team and a trusted strategic partner in advancing this work. They will manage a significant portfolio while working with the Vice President of External Affairs to translate strategic priorities into staff assignments, timelines and deliverables, coordinate workflow across the team, monitor progress, and ensure consistent execution and follow through. They will be expected to exercise significant independent judgment and represent the Federation with elected officials, faith and civic leaders, educational institutions, community organizations and other stakeholders.

Miami-Dade County is home to one of the largest, most diverse and fastest-growing Jewish communities in the United States. The community exists within a dynamic civic environment at the intersection of local, statewide, national and international issues. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment and will possess the judgment, intellectual curiosity and interpersonal skills necessary to build meaningful relationships across political, religious, ethnic and cultural differences both within and outside the Jewish community.

The JCRC Deputy Director reports to the Vice President of External Affairs.

**Join us to build a long-term, rewarding, and fulfilling career!**

***Essential Functions and Responsibilities***

· Serve as a senior strategic partner to the Vice President of External Affairs in developing and implementing the JCRC’s priorities, programs, advocacy agenda and external engagement strategy.

· Manage a significant portfolio of internal and external relationships, including elected officials and government partners at the local, state and federal levels, as well as faith, ethnic, cultural and civic leaders and organizations; maintain and deepen key relationships, identify new partnership and coalition-building opportunities, coordinate meetings and briefings, develop joint programs and initiatives, and advance JCRC advocacy and community-relations priorities.

· Expand the JCRC’s bridge-building and coalition-building capabilities, with particular emphasis on developing meaningful relationships with Spanish-speaking non-Jewish community leaders and identifying new communities and constituencies with whom the Federation should engage.

· Broaden the JCRC’s external reach and influence by strengthening relationships with local and national journalists, identifying opportunities for proactive media engagement, and cultivating relationships with digital influencers and other voices who can help deepen understanding of antisemitism, Israel and the Jewish community.

· Help shape and execute JCRC messaging and communications across traditional and digital platforms, ensuring that complex and sensitive issues are communicated accurately, strategically and effectively to audiences with varying levels of knowledge and differing perspectives.

· Oversee key aspects of the JCRC’s day-to-day operations, translating strategic priorities into staff assignments, timelines and deliverables; coordinating workflow across the team; monitoring progress; and ensuring consistent execution and follow-through; and assuming increasing leadership responsibility as familiarity with JCRC, Federation and community grows.

· Directly supervise assigned JCRC professional staff, including setting priorities and expectations, providing regular feedback and coaching, monitoring performance and supporting professional development.

· Develop and track meaningful metrics and key performance indicators to evaluate the effectiveness of JCRC programs, relationships and initiatives; use data and analysis to inform strategy, strengthen decision-making and demonstrate impact to Federation leadership, donors, foundations, elected officials and community partners.

· Identify emerging opportunities, challenges and trends affecting the Jewish community and recommend proactive strategies for addressing them.

· Help lead the JCRC’s response to emerging community issues and crises, working across Federation departments and with external partners to coordinate strategy, communications and action.

· Help guide JCRC efforts to prevent, address and respond to antisemitism and anti-Jewish bias, including developing proactive strategies that deepen understanding of antisemitism, strengthen alliances and build resilience within the Jewish community.

· Maintain a strong working knowledge of Israel, Israeli society, the U.S.-Israel relationship and developments affecting Israel and the Jewish people, and serve as a knowledgeable resource for Federation leadership, community partners and external stakeholders.

· Build strong relationships with JCRC lay leaders, Federation volunteers and donors, and partner with them to advance strategic priorities, strengthen committee and task-force engagement, and cultivate emerging leaders who can expand the JCRC’s reach within the Jewish and broader communities.

· Represent the Federation at meetings, public programs, community events, coalitions and other external forums, including speaking publicly on behalf of the JCRC when appropriate.

· Take ownership of special projects and emerging priorities as assigned by the Vice President of External Affair

jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
**Work with Us**
================

Peoria Riverfront Museum offers a variety of benefits including a team-oriented environment, 403b/Roth option with employer match, free employee parking, an array of museum discounts and, for full-time staff: health, dental, vision and life insurance, healthcare and dependent care flexible spending program, and a competitive time-off program.

  

### **Director of Marketing and Communications**

#### **M-F, 9-5p (flexible as needed to meet deadlines or attend meetings or special events)**

#### **Salary Range: $65,000 - $70,000**

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads the development and execution of the Museum’s comprehensive external marketing and communications strategy. This role drives brand awareness, audience engagement, attendance growth, media visibility, and revenue support.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director oversees media relations, advertising, digital strategy, website management, social media, graphic design, and all external communications. The role also leads the marketing team, manages budgets, evaluates campaign performance, and ensures that every public-facing message reflects the excellence and innovation of the Museum.

#### **What You’ll Do:**

##### **Brand and Content Excellence**

* Lead the creation and curation of compelling content across print, digital, video, and social platforms.
* Oversee production of brochures, publications, website content, social campaigns, signage, photography, and multimedia assets.
* Ensure brand consistency and high visual standards across all channels.
* Ensure marketing materials meet accessibility standards and reflect the Museum's commitment to serving diverse audiences.

##### **Digital and Media Presence**

* Manage the Museum’s website strategy, design, and maintenance to ensure a dynamic and user-friendly experience.
* Drive social media engagement and digital storytelling initiatives.
* Cultivate strong relationships with local, regional, and national media to secure impactful coverage.

##### **Advertising and Vendor Management**

* Strategically purchase and manage advertising across traditional and digital platforms.
* Oversee relationships with creative agencies, designers, printers, and other vendors.

##### **Measurement and Impact**

* Implement evaluation tools to measure marketing effectiveness.
* Analyze data, interpret campaign results, and adjust strategy for maximum impact.
* Align marketing performance with institutional goals for attendance, membership, and revenue.

##### **Team and Department Leadership**

* Lead a highly performing team and oversee day-to-day operations of the Marketing and Communications Department.
* Lead budgeting, planning, staff supervision, and professional development.
* Oversee departmental hiring, performance management, coaching, disciplinary action and annual evaluations.
* Collaborate with the COO and Director of Finance to develop and manage the annual marketing budget.

#### **What We’re Looking For:**

You are both strategist and storyteller. You understand how to translate mission into message and ideas into action. You thrive in fast-paced, creative environments and bring energy, organization, and leadership to everything you do.

* Bachelor’s degree required (Journalism, Communications, Marketing, or related field preferred).
* Minimum five years of experience writing and editing across print and digital platforms.
* Demonstrated success developing and implementing marketing strategies with measurable results.
* Exceptional writing, editing, and visual storytelling skills.
* Strong knowledge of local, regional, and national media landscapes.
* Experience managing advertising and vendor relationships.
* Ability to evaluate and integrate innovative media technologies.
* Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines.
* Collaborative leadership style with supervisory experience preferred.
* Nonprofit experience preferred.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and standard business applications.

#### **Work Environment and Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to work in a standard office environment using computers and other office equipment for extended periods.
* Visual acuity for reviewing detailed creative work.
* Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and in writing.
* Ability to move throughout the Museum and event spaces to attend meetings and support programs and special events.
* Ability to occasionally lift and carry materials weighing up to 30 pounds.
* Ability to work evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed to support Museum operations and events.
* Ability to travel occasionally for meetings, conferences, and professional development.

#### **Why You’ll Love Working Here:**

The Peoria Riverfront Museum is a cultural catalyst creating transformative experiences for our community. As the only museum in the country to unite art, science, history, and achievement in a single institution of its scale, we are redefining what a museum can be.

As Director of Marketing and Communications, you will not just promote programs—you will help shape the cultural narrative of an entire region.

If you are ready to lead boldly, think creatively, and make measurable impact, we invite you to apply.

**PITTSBURGH BALLET THEATRE**

**Director of Development**

  

**REPORTS TO:** Executive Director

**DATE:** October 2026  
**DEPARTMENT:** Administration  
**STATUS:** Full-time, FLSA Exempt  
**SALAY:** Starting at $125,000  
  
**ABOUT PITTSBURGH BALLET THEATRE (PBT)**:  
Founded in 1969, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre’s mission is to be Pittsburgh’s source and ambassador for extraordinary ballet experiences that give life to the classical tradition, nurture new ideas and, above all, inspire. PBT provides high-caliber ballet performances and rich educational opportunities to audiences in the downtown Cultural District and in community-based settings throughout the Pittsburgh region. The company is known for its bold, athletic, and adventurous artistic vision, as well as for its diverse repertoire of classics and new works. PBT is committed to building an organizational culture of inclusivity, collaboration and innovation.  
  
**POSITION SUMMARY**  
The Director of Development will serve as Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre’s lead fundraiser and oversee all development efforts. The successful candidate will have a proven record of collaborating with executive leadership, boards, committees, and other key stakeholders to foster a culture of philanthropy and implement comprehensive fundraising strategies that expand and engage a diverse donor base.  
  
The Director of Development will be skilled in major-gift cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship; the planning and execution of fundraising and donor-engagement events; and serving as a compelling ambassador and spokesperson for PBT.  
  
Key Internal Relationships: Holds accountability to both the Executive Director and Artistic Director and serves as a key member of the senior leadership team. Leads and manages the Development team and works closely with the Board of Trustees and its Development Committee. jobs.description:
**VCP PROVIDES EXCELLENT BENEFITS!!**

* **Employees pay $0 out-of-pocket towards health,** **vision and dental premiums**
* **VCP offers a 401k plan at a 4% match**
* **Employees receive** **6 weeks of paid time off in addition to major holidays**

**Veterans Community Project (VCP) Overview**

VCP was founded in Kansas City, Missouri, in 2016 by a group of combat Veterans shaped by their military service and began with a determination to do better for Veterans in need. Today, we’re growing nationwide to serve more Veterans everywhere, ensuring no one is left behind. Our founders’ solution was simple: provide Veterans experiencing homelessness with a home of their own and wraparound case management services that leverage the support of the community to not only get them back on their feet, but ensure they continue standing. Our proven model has an 85% success rate at getting Veterans back on their feet.

**The Team**

We, the team members and co-founders of VCP, operate with innovation, entrepreneurism, and grit in our mission to serve those who served. We move with swift, bold action, driven by purpose. We believe in collaboration, community, compassion, and above all, serving Veterans with dignity and respect. We serve all Veterans with that ethos—regardless of length or type of service, or discharge status.

**The Role**

Are you a visionary fundraiser with a passion for transforming generosity into impact? As the Director of Development, you will serve as a member of the local leadership team and the leader of local development efforts. Under the direction of the local Executive Director and in strong collaboration with the National Director of Philanthropy, she/he initiates and implements development strategies, planning, and activities that result in a compelling, donor-centered development program which invites our community-at-large to have a lasting relationship with VCP to achieve our goals.

She/he will serve as a major gift officer, managing and cultivating relationships with existing major gift prospects, as well as identifying new prospects; interact with individuals and senior members of corporations/foundations; ensure local fundraising goals are met; work in direct collaboration with local fundraising consultant and leadership team; may serve as a liaison with other organizations’ staff when VCP is involved in joint ventures; supervise the development staff to include recommending staff hires, discipline, performance management, and day-to-day supervision of the department.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* With the Executive Director & National Director of Philanthropy, you will develop and implement an integrated development program using a variety of cultivation, solicitation and stewardship techniques including making personal visits, and phone calls, sending appeals, events and gatherings, online campaigns, and networking. Includes helping unleash the giving potential of a wide array of funders and stakeholders and ensure that annual fundraising goals are met.

* Manage the local day-to-day development operations including prospect identification and research; cultivation and communications strategies; proposal development; writing, submission, and tracking of grants; solicitation strategies; donor stewardship, donor-centered communication, and outreach activities; and community engagement/volunteer relations.

* Provide leadership in research, qualification, and cultivation of prospective donors. Determine readiness of donors to progress toward giving and deeper engagement with VCP.

* Plan, coordinate, prepare materials, and participate in meetings to cultivate and solicit prospective donors and community partners; research new sponsorship options using appropriate cultivation activities.

* Together with the National Director of Philanthropy, National Director of Marketing, and the Marketing & Donor Relations Manager, ensure a meaningful donor stewardship plan is in place and implemented to achieve maximum donor loyalty and develop marketing strategies to promote the VCP image.

* Participate in annual budget preparation, including making revenue projections and goal setting.

* Foster relationships with other VCP departments and development team members in other cities to build a cooperative and effective program that promotes a culture of philanthropy.

* Responsible for the overall coordination and execution of local capital campaign initiatives, providing strategic leadership and oversight of the Capital Campaign Committee to ensure goals are met and community engagement is maximized.

**Competencies and Areas of Expertise may Include:**

* Passion for the mission of VCP.

* Bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, non-profit management, or a related field or equivalent educational experience.

* Seven – ten years progressively responsible related experience; or any combination of education, training and experience, that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the essential functions of the job. Work experience preferably in non-profit environment.

* Advanced understanding of the principles of fundraising; current issues and trends in fundraising; corporate social responsibility; marketing; fiscal management; and volunteer management.

* Experience in grant writing as well as major giving (individual and corporate), portfolio/moves management.

* Exceptional interpersonal skills with emphasis on building relationships and asking for gifts.

* Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to develop and deliver compelling arguments regarding the value proposition of VCP. Experience in donor-centric communication preferred.

* Knowledge of a non-profit donor CRM is required (ie: Raiser’s Edge, NEON, Virtuous, etc.)

* Advanced knowledge of technical computer skills in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and social networking, including ability to utilize technology for research.

Breakthrough Denver, a program of Kent Denver School

**LOCATION:**

Englewood, Colorado

Head of School or designee

**ADVISORY PARTNER:**

Breakthrough Denver Advisory Board

**JOB CATEGORY:**

Full-Time, Year-Round (Exempt)

**PROGRAM REACH:**

More than 450 students in grades 7 through 12, as well as post-secondary

  

**OVERVIEW:**

The Breakthrough Denver Executive Director is an accomplished, mission-driven leader who guides a high-impact, year-round program serving more than 450 motivated, historically underrepresented students in grades 7 through 12 who are pursuing post-secondary opportunities, as well as preparing talented college students for careers in education. The Executive Director will build on a strong program model and a long-standing partnership with Kent Denver School to ensure excellent student outcomes, a healthy and inclusive organizational culture, durable community relationships, and sustainable philanthropic support.

The Executive Director is accountable for Breakthrough Denver's overall leadership, quality, and sustainability. The Director sets direction; translates strategy into measurable annual priorities; develops and supports the staff; safeguards the student and Teaching Fellow experience; leads fundraising and external relations; and stewards the program's financial and operational resources. Success requires equal strength in educational leadership, organizational management, relationship building, strategic philanthropy, fundraising and execution.

This is a distinctive leadership role. Breakthrough Denver is not a separate nonprofit corporation; it is a program hosted by Kent Denver School and an affiliate of Breakthrough Collaborative. The Executive Director, therefore, leads Breakthrough Denver with substantial programmatic and external responsibilities while working within Kent Denver's legal, financial, human resources, safety, and risk management framework. The Executive Director also partners closely with the Breakthrough Denver Advisory Board, whose role is to support and sustain the program through fundraising, advocacy, relationships, and program support.

  

**JOB DESCRIPTION:**

Strategic and Organizational Leadership
---------------------------------------

* Develop and execute a clear, multi-year strategy aligned with Breakthrough Denver's mission, Kent Denver School's institutional priorities, and Breakthrough Collaborative's affiliate expectations.
* Translate strategy into annual goals, work plans, budgets, performance measures, and clear accountability across the team.
* Use student, program, financial, and stakeholder data to assess results, identify risks and opportunities, and improve the program continuously.
* Serve as the senior advocate for Breakthrough Denver within Kent Denver and as the program's principal representative in the broader community.

Program Quality and Student Success
-----------------------------------

* Ensure coherent, high-quality summer and school-year programming from entry after sixth grade through high school graduation and college matriculation.
* Establish ambitious, developmentally appropriate outcomes for academic growth, high school success, college readiness, student belonging, and persistence; monitor progress and respond to findings.
* Center the experiences and aspirations of students and families in program design, evaluation, communication, and decision making.
* Oversee the recruitment, selection, training, coaching, and performance of Teaching Fellows and seasonal instructional staff in collaboration with program leaders.
* Maintain strong systems for student safety, supervision, attendance, behavior support, transportation, communication, and emergency response in accordance with Kent Denver policies.

Team Leadership and Culture
---------------------------

* Recruit, retain, supervise, coach, and evaluate a talented year-round and seasonal team, with clear roles, goals, feedback, and opportunities for professional growth.
* Foster a culture of trust, high expectations, collaboration, belonging, learning, and shared responsibility for results.
* Plan staffing and organizational capacity to meet year-round and summer program needs, in accordance with Kent Denver's employment and human resources practices.

Fundraising and External Relations
----------------------------------

* Serve as the program's lead fundraiser and, with staff, Kent Denver partners, and the Advisory Board, build and execute an annual and multi-year development strategy as well as annual fundraising events.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward individuals, foundations, corporations, and other partners; develop compelling proposals, reports, site visits, events, and donor communications.
* Build a diverse and sustainable funding base sufficient to support current operations, appropriate reserves, and thoughtfully planned growth.
* Communicate Breakthrough Denver's mission, outcomes, and needs with clarity and integrity, honoring the dignity and agency of students and families.
* Develop productive partnerships with public schools, community organizations, colleges and universities, education leaders, and other stakeholders

Financial and Operational Stewardship
-------------------------------------

* Develop and manage the annual program budget, monitor revenue and expenses, forecast needs, and provide timely, accurate reporting to Kent Denver leadership and the Advisory Board.
* Work closely with Kent Denver's finance, advancement, human resources, facilities, technology, communications, and risk management teams; follow applicable school policies and approval processes.
* Maintain effective systems, records, controls, contracts, data practices, and vendor relationships that support efficient operations and protect students, families, employees, volunteers, and the institution.
* Fulfill Breakthrough Collaborative affiliate obligations and draw strategically on the national net

**Director of Communications**

Healthcare is increasingly unaffordable for many Americans. Most people believe they have two choices: increasingly expensive, restrictive employer insurance, or an ACA plan that keeps getting pricier. Many don't know there's a third, smarter option.

**WeShare Health** is that option.

WeShare Health’s mission is to make healthcare simpler, more affordable, and more human. We're a nonprofit, faith-inspired healthcare sharing organization where members contribute monthly to share one another's eligible medical expenses. We're proudly not insurance, and that's the point.

Members access a national network of 1 million physicians at 30 to 60 percent less than comparable traditional insurance. Since 2018, WeShare Health has served more than 100,000 members and shared more than $50 million in medical expenses. Our purpose is clear: people before profit.

WeShare Health is led by senior executives with deep experience across for-profit and nonprofit enterprises. We’re rated 4.6 out of 5 on Google Reviews, rated 4.7 on Trustpilot by members and certified as a Great Place To Work® by our employees. If you have a bias for action, enjoy challenges, and want to disrupt the status quo to make an impact in a massive industry, WeShare Health might be the place for you!

**About the Role**

The Director of Public Relations is a hands-on builder who helps create WeShare Health's PR function. Reporting to the VP of Marketing Communications, you will help build and run the processes, tools, and playbooks that power our earned media and thought leadership programs.

The ideal candidate brings a strong mix of consumer and healthcare PR experience with the versatility to engage a diverse media and stakeholder landscape: healthcare trade press, regional and national consumer media, and business outlets, on behalf of a mission that genuinely matters.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop pitch strategies and story angles that generate meaningful coverage across healthcare trade, business, and regional and national consumer media
* Identify news cycles, policy developments, and white-space opportunities to insert WeShare Health into relevant conversations
* Write and manage content across blogs, LinkedIn, executive bylines, and internal communications
* Support crisis communications planning and response
* Activate and maintain PR infrastructure: editorial calendars, media databases, coverage tracking, messaging frameworks, and agency management protocols
* Co-create KPIs and reporting that connect coverage, share of voice, and sentiment to business impact

 **Qualifications:**  
  
**Required**

* 6+ years of progressive PR or communications experience
* Track record of securing earned media in national, regional, and trade publications
* Strong writing skills, with the ability to mirror different executive voices
* Experience managing PR agencies or consultants
* Ability to work effectively in a matrixed environment without direct authority
* Builder's mindset and a positive, team-player orientation

  
**Preferred**

* Experience with Reddit, LinkedIn or community-platform engagement
* Experience in digital health or health insurance

  
**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and vision insurance, 403(b) with company match
* Ability to make important enhancements to the Healthcare industry.
* Great culture where you work with the founders and key stakeholders in a relaxed, but innovative atmosphere.

**New York Center for Interpersonal Development (NYCID)**

We believe in building community and nurturing personal growth. We improve lives through effective communication, conflict management, social-emotional learning, and youth development. Through our core values of Collaboration, Accountability Recognition, and Resilience, NYCID works to help people develop skills which move New York City toward the goal of being a more civil and economically stable place for all.

**Department Overview**

NYCID collaborates with interested New York City Public Schools (NYCPS) to develop, customize, and implement self-sustaining and/or funded After School programs. Our programs can be operated in any elementary, middle, or high school, and are designed to enrich students’ academic, social, and emotional development. We work collaboratively with schools to tailor our programs to meet the unique needs of each school and its community.

Our goal is to provide enrichment opportunities that expose students to subjects and experiences they may not otherwise encounter outside of the school environment. These may include arts, STEM, leadership development, cultural exploration, fitness and wellness, and college and career readiness. In addition, our programs offer opportunities for youth to learn conflict resolution, anger management, and decision-making techniques.

We approach our work through a youth development framework, giving our undivided attention and commitment to both our students and their families to foster growth, engagement, and lasting impact.

**SONYC Program**

SONYC Programs are funded by the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) and are structured like clubs to offer young people choice in how they spend their time. This After School program is for students in middle school. SONYC offers a wide range of activities such as Dance and Music, Sports and Fitness, Literacy, Art, Culinary Arts, and Fashion and Design. There is also a strong focus on STEAM and Leadership activities which are led by professional staff.

COMPASS is also funded by DYCD and serves young students in grades K through 5. Through its network of providers, COMPASS NYC offers high-quality programs that balance academics, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of young people. Students who participate have the opportunity to explore their interests, express their creativity, and build skills that support their academic achievement, boost their confidence, and encourage personal growth.

**Position Specification**

The Stimson Center is a nonprofit, nonpartisan, independent, and action-oriented research and policy organization
  
committed to enhancing international security and prosperity through pragmatic solutions to the world's most difficult
  
challenges. Founded in 1989 by Michael Krepon and Barry Blechman, Stimson has built a distinctive reputation for
  
bringing rigorous research, policy expertise, and creative problem-solving to issues where traditional approaches often
  
fall short. Stimson's programs work individually and in tandem in the relentless pursuit of a more peaceful, secure, and
  
prosperous world.

The international system is undergoing profound change. Intensifying geopolitical competition, the erosion of
  
longstanding norms and institutions, emerging technologies, and increasingly interconnected security challenges are
  
creating new risks while complicating the pathways to cooperation. In this environment, Stimson's ability to work
  
across divides, anticipate emerging challenges, and translate independent analysis into practical policy solutions is
  
increasingly critical.

With a global body of work spanning more than 20 programs, Stimson brings together experts across disciplines and
  
regions to tackle complex problems with an emphasis on practical solutions and measurable impact. Its work spans
  
nuclear security and nonproliferation, Indo-Pacific dynamics, regional security, emerging technologies, climate and
  
security, and international governance. Across these areas, Stimson looks beyond conventional approaches to identify
  
emerging risks, challenge assumptions, and develop ideas that can be translated into policy and practical application
  
for measurable impact.

For decades, Stimson has served as a critical bridge between policymakers, governments, military leaders,
  
international institutions, civil society, academia, and the private sector. From military-to-military dialogues and
  
international convenings to rigorous research and policy engagement, Stimson creates trusted spaces for candid
  
conversation and constructive problem-solving - often when official relationships are under strain and the need for
  
independent, credible interlocutors is greatest.

Stimson's impact is grounded in its ability to combine intellectual independence with practical engagement. Its experts
  
are regularly called upon by governments, international organizations, the media, and other leading institutions for
  
analysis and insight on emerging global security challenges. The organization is committed to anticipating global risk
  
as well as responding to emerging crises, with a demonstrated capacity for building the connections and partnerships
  
capable of advancing durable solutions.

Stimson's independence is central to its value. Free from the influence or constraints of outside forces, Stimson can
  
interrogate long-held assumptions, bring unexpected voices together, and engage across political and national
  
divides. Its combination of intellectual rigor, agile activity, and trusted relationships allows the organization to operate
  
where few others can.

As Stimson looks to its next chapter, the organization is well positioned to build on this history while adapting to a
  
rapidly changing global environment. Its challenge - and opportunity - is to sustain the independence, credibility,
  
and collaborative spirit that have defined Stimson while expanding its reach, impact, and financial sustainability. With
  
a strong foundation of expertise, trusted relationships, and a reputation for fierce nonpartisanship, Stimson is
  
positioned to play an important role in helping decisionmakers at all levels navigate an increasingly complex and
  
consequential world.

The next President and CEO will have the opportunity to build on Stimson's distinctive legacy while helping define its
  
next chapter - strengthening its programs and people, expanding its reach and partnerships, and ensuring the
  
organization has the resources and institutional capacity to meet the challenges ahead. The leader will inherit an
  
organization with a clear sense of purpose and a distinctive role to play at a consequential moment for global security.

Stimson's Board of Directors is comprised of 20-25 individuals providing trusted counsel to the organization from
  
around the world. Stimson's Board provides a strategic mix of experience and perspectives, including representatives
  
across government, private sector, philanthropy, technology, law, defense, and diplomacy.
  
The Stimson Center has 75+ full-time staff, based in Washington, DC, and an annual budget of $16-18 million USD
  
per year.

To learn more about the Stimson Center and its work, please visit https://www.stimson.org/.

Based in Washington, D.C. and working in close partnership with the Board of Directors and the Executive Team, the
  
President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will lead the Stimson Center and hold responsibility for its institutional
  
direction, programmatic impact, financial health, and organizational effectiveness. The next CEO will inherit a well  
respected institution that has grown significantly in scope and size recently, with a reputation for rigorous analysis, a

new_jobs.title: Deputy Director, Jewish Community Relations Council
new_jobs.description:
Department: Jewish Community Relations Council

Location: Miami, FL

Employment Type: Full-time / Exempt / Hybrid

***Job Description Summary***

The Greater Miami Jewish Federation seeks a strategic, relationship-driven and highly motivated professional to serve as Deputy Director of its Jewish Community Relations Council (JCRC).

The JCRC serves as the public affairs and community relations arm of the Greater Miami Jewish Federation, building relationships and coalitions that strengthen the Jewish community, combat antisemitism, deepen understanding of Israel and the Jewish people, and advance the Jewish community’s interests and values in the broader civic community.

The Deputy Director will serve as a senior operational lead of the JCRC team and a trusted strategic partner in advancing this work. They will manage a significant portfolio while working with the Vice President of External Affairs to translate strategic priorities into staff assignments, timelines and deliverables, coordinate workflow across the team, monitor progress, and ensure consistent execution and follow through. They will be expected to exercise significant independent judgment and represent the Federation with elected officials, faith and civic leaders, educational institutions, community organizations and other stakeholders.

Miami-Dade County is home to one of the largest, most diverse and fastest-growing Jewish communities in the United States. The community exists within a dynamic civic environment at the intersection of local, statewide, national and international issues. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment and will possess the judgment, intellectual curiosity and interpersonal skills necessary to build meaningful relationships across political, religious, ethnic and cultural differences both within and outside the Jewish community.

The JCRC Deputy Director reports to the Vice President of External Affairs.

**Join us to build a long-term, rewarding, and fulfilling career!**

***Essential Functions and Responsibilities***

· Serve as a senior strategic partner to the Vice President of External Affairs in developing and implementing the JCRC’s priorities, programs, advocacy agenda and external engagement strategy.

· Manage a significant portfolio of internal and external relationships, including elected officials and government partners at the local, state and federal levels, as well as faith, ethnic, cultural and civic leaders and organizations; maintain and deepen key relationships, identify new partnership and coalition-building opportunities, coordinate meetings and briefings, develop joint programs and initiatives, and advance JCRC advocacy and community-relations priorities.

· Expand the JCRC’s bridge-building and coalition-building capabilities, with particular emphasis on developing meaningful relationships with Spanish-speaking non-Jewish community leaders and identifying new communities and constituencies with whom the Federation should engage.

· Broaden the JCRC’s external reach and influence by strengthening relationships with local and national journalists, identifying opportunities for proactive media engagement, and cultivating relationships with digital influencers and other voices who can help deepen understanding of antisemitism, Israel and the Jewish community.

· Help shape and execute JCRC messaging and communications across traditional and digital platforms, ensuring that complex and sensitive issues are communicated accurately, strategically and effectively to audiences with varying levels of knowledge and differing perspectives.

· Oversee key aspects of the JCRC’s day-to-day operations, translating strategic priorities into staff assignments, timelines and deliverables; coordinating workflow across the team; monitoring progress; and ensuring consistent execution and follow-through; and assuming increasing leadership responsibility as familiarity with JCRC, Federation and community grows.

· Directly supervise assigned JCRC professional staff, including setting priorities and expectations, providing regular feedback and coaching, monitoring performance and supporting professional development.

· Develop and track meaningful metrics and key performance indicators to evaluate the effectiveness of JCRC programs, relationships and initiatives; use data and analysis to inform strategy, strengthen decision-making and demonstrate impact to Federation leadership, donors, foundations, elected officials and community partners.

· Identify emerging opportunities, challenges and trends affecting the Jewish community and recommend proactive strategies for addressing them.

· Help lead the JCRC’s response to emerging community issues and crises, working across Federation departments and with external partners to coordinate strategy, communications and action.

· Help guide JCRC efforts to prevent, address and respond to antisemitism and anti-Jewish bias, including developing proactive strategies that deepen understanding of antisemitism, strengthen alliances and build resilience within the Jewish community.

· Maintain a strong working knowledge of Israel, Israeli society, the U.S.-Israel relationship and developments affecting Israel and the Jewish people, and serve as a knowledgeable resource for Federation leadership, community partners and external stakeholders.

· Build strong relationships with JCRC lay leaders, Federation volunteers and donors, and partner with them to advance strategic priorities, strengthen committee and task-force engagement, and cultivate emerging leaders who can expand the JCRC’s reach within the Jewish and broader communities.

· Represent the Federation at meetings, public programs, community events, coalitions and other external forums, including speaking publicly on behalf of the JCRC when appropriate.

· Take ownership of special projects and emerging priorities as assigned by the Vice President of External Affair

new_jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
new_jobs.description:
**Work with Us**
================

Peoria Riverfront Museum offers a variety of benefits including a team-oriented environment, 403b/Roth option with employer match, free employee parking, an array of museum discounts and, for full-time staff: health, dental, vision and life insurance, healthcare and dependent care flexible spending program, and a competitive time-off program.

  

### **Director of Marketing and Communications**

#### **M-F, 9-5p (flexible as needed to meet deadlines or attend meetings or special events)**

#### **Salary Range: $65,000 - $70,000**

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads the development and execution of the Museum’s comprehensive external marketing and communications strategy. This role drives brand awareness, audience engagement, attendance growth, media visibility, and revenue support.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director oversees media relations, advertising, digital strategy, website management, social media, graphic design, and all external communications. The role also leads the marketing team, manages budgets, evaluates campaign performance, and ensures that every public-facing message reflects the excellence and innovation of the Museum.

#### **What You’ll Do:**

* Manage the Museum’s website strategy, design, and maintenance to ensure a dynamic and user-friendly experience.

* Strategically purchase and manage advertising across traditional and digital platforms.

##### **Measurement and Impact**

* Implement evaluation tools to measure marketing effectiveness.
* Analyze data, interpret campaign results, and adjust strategy for maximum impact.
* Align marketing performance with institutional goals for attendance, membership, and revenue.

##### **Team and Department Leadership**

* Lead a highly performing team and oversee day-to-day operations of the Marketing and Communications Department.
* Lead budgeting, planning, staff supervision, and professional development.
* Oversee departmental hiring, performance management, coaching, disciplinary action and annual evaluations.
* Collaborate with the COO and Director of Finance to develop and manage the annual marketing budget.

#### **What We’re Looking For:**

You are both strategist and storyteller. You understand how to translate mission into message and ideas into action. You thrive in fast-paced, creative environments and bring energy, organization, and leadership to everything you do.

* Bachelor’s degree required (Journalism, Communications, Marketing, or related field preferred).
* Minimum five years of experience writing and editing across print and digital platforms.
* Demonstrated success developing and implementing marketing strategies with measurable results.
* Exceptional writing, editing, and visual storytelling skills.
* Strong knowledge of local, regional, and national media landscapes.
* Experience managing advertising and vendor relationships.
* Ability to evaluate and integrate innovative media technologies.
* Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines.
* Collaborative leadership style with supervisory experience preferred.
* Nonprofit experience preferred.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and standard business applications.

#### **Work Environment and Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to work in a standard office environment using computers and other office equipment for extended periods.
* Visual acuity for reviewing detailed creative work.
* Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and in writing.
* Ability to move throughout the Museum and event spaces to attend meetings and support programs and special events.
* Ability to occasionally lift and carry materials weighing up to 30 pounds.
* Ability to work evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed to support Museum operations and events.
* Ability to travel occasionally for meetings, conferences, and professional development.

#### **Why You’ll Love Working Here:**

The Peoria Riverfront Museum is a cultural catalyst creating transformative experiences for our community. As the only museum in the country to unite art, science, history, and achievement in a single institution of its scale, we are redefining what a museum can be.

As Director of Marketing and Communications, you will not just promote programs—you will help shape the cultural narrative of an entire region.

If you are ready to lead boldly, think creatively, and make measurable impact, we invite you to apply.

**ABOUT PITTSBURGH BALLET THEATRE (PBT)**:  
Founded in 1969, Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre’s mission is to be Pittsburgh’s source and ambassador for extraordinary ballet experiences that give life to the classical tradition, nurture new ideas and, above all, inspire. PBT provides high-caliber ballet performances and rich educational opportunities to audiences in the downtown Cultural District and in community-based settings throughout the Pittsburgh region. The company is known for its bold, athletic, and adventurous artistic vision, as well as for its diverse repertoire of classics and new works. PBT is committed to building an organizational culture of inclusivity, collaboration and innovation.  
  
**POSITION SUMMARY**  
The Director of Development will serve as Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre’s lead fundraiser and oversee all development efforts. The successful candidate will have a proven record of collaborating with executive leadership, boards, committees, and other key stakeholders to foster a culture of philanthropy and implement comprehensive fundraising strategies that expand and engage a diverse donor base.

**COMPETENCIES, SKILLS, AND QUALIFICATIONS**

**WHY PBT**

Our founders’ solution was simple: provide Veterans experiencing homelessness with a home of their own and wraparound case management services that leverage the support of the community to not only get them back on their feet, but ensure they continue standing. Our proven model has an 85% success rate at getting Veterans back on their feet.

Overview:

Presbyterian Homes & Services is seeking a **Director of Philanthropy** to join their Foundation Team. This position will office from both the Home Office in Roseville, MN, and may also office at one of our communities.

The Director of Philanthropy provides strategic leadership for major gift, gift planning, and campaign fundraising activities across Presbyterian Homes & Services communities and service lines. Serving as the Foundation's senior fundraising strategist and practitioner, this role works collaboratively with Foundation leadership, community leaders, residents, families, professional advisors, and donors to identify philanthropic opportunities that advance organizational priorities.

The Director leads and develops the Foundation's team of Gift Planning Officers, manages a select portfolio of leadership-level donors and prospects, and serves as the Foundation's primary resource for solicitation planning, gift planning expertise, and fundraising best practices.

Responsibilities:

The Director of Philanthropy reports to the Vice President, Foundation and directly supervises and develops a geographically dispersed team of Gift Planning Officers and other fundraising staff as assigned.

Key Responsibilities included but are not limited to:

* Develop, lead, and evaluate Foundation fundraising strategy for major gift, planned gift, and campaign efforts across PHS communities and service lines.
* Serve as a member of the Foundation leadership team, contributing to strategic planning, staffing decisions, budgets, and revenue forecasts.
* Personally manage a portfolio of leadership-level donors and prospects, securing at least $1M in major and planned gift commitments annually.
* Lead the Gift Planning Officer team to established metrics, including annual goals of at least $500,000 in major gift revenue and six documented planned gift commitments per year.
* Establish and maintain moves management standards, ensuring qualified portfolios of 100–120 prospects and at least four qualification visits per month with new portfolio prospects.
* Drive qualified pipeline growth, accurate revenue forecasting, and campaign performance against goals set with the Vice President, Foundation.
* Serve as the Foundation's primary internal resource for charitable gift planning, supporting complex gifts involving estates, trusts, annuities, beneficiary designations, real estate, securities, and other non-cash assets.
* Build relationships with attorneys, financial advisors, accountants, trust officers, and other professional advisors; support estate planning seminars and Legacy Society growth.
* Provide strategic leadership for, and lead implementation of, capital campaigns, endowment campaigns, community initiatives, and special fundraising projects in partnership with executive and campus leadership.
* Recruit, hire, onboard, coach, develop, and evaluate Gift Planning Officers and other assigned staff, fostering a collaborative, donor-centered culture.
* Support the integration of Christian culture and heritage through communication and education systems.

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or relevant professional designation (CFRE, CAP®, CFP®) preferred.

* Proven success personally securing major and planned gifts, including outright, deferred, blended, and complex gifts.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Program Director to lead our Behavioral Health Clinic, championing mental health and behavioral care excellence. This pivotal role involves overseeing clinical operations, supervising multidisciplinary teams, and ensuring the delivery of compassionate, evidence-based services to diverse populations. The ideal candidate will be passionate about improving patient outcomes, and adept at managing complex cases involving mental health, substance use disorders, neurodevelopmental disabilities, and co-occurring conditions.
